title: A Choir for the Spire
premise: Ivo Montrose, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics he carves, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things — a trade in relics, oaths, and debts that should not exist. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Ivo discovers she is the last living word of a broken covenant between the human realms and the dragon-fire that once sealed it. Hunted by guild rivals and a crown inquisitor who wants the covenant dead for good, Ivo and an unlikely found family must carry the child to the Spire where the last flame gutters out. In the end, Ivo pays the price of survival by giving up his own voice to the fire, reforging the covenant with the child as its new speaker — love against duty, answered at last.
about_author: Sable Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing broken oaths in municipal records before turning to fantasy. They write about debt, grief, and the families we carve out of strangers.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A quiet night in the Guild house: Ivo carves a dead woman's knucklebone and hears her last confession, establishing his gift and his loneliness among colleagues who treat him as a tool. Emotional beat: competent isolation — he belongs to the ledgers, not to people.

chapters.title: A Word Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A mud-soaked child appears at the Guild door during a storm, speaking a language no one knows — until Ivo touches her carved amulet and hears the dead dragons answering. The Guild master orders her locked away as inventory. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered through Ivo's translations). Locked in the vault, the child — Wren — shows Ivo fragments of memory: burning spires, a dying pact. Meanwhile the crown inquisitor Halvard arrives demanding 'the anomaly.' Emotional beat: two prisoners recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. To protect Wren from Halvard, Ivo falsifies the ledgers — erasing her entry, a hanging offense. His mentor Odile covers for him but warns him the Guild always collects its debts. Emotional beat: first act of love disguised as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Bone Market
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Ivo and Wren. Halvard raids the Guild; Odile dies buying their escape, her death heard through the bone in Ivo's pocket. They flee into the black market with a smuggler, Tamsin, who owes Ivo an old favor. Emotional beat: grief converted into momentum.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the road, Wren begins teaching Ivo her language; each word unlocks a dragon-memory showing how the covenant broke — humans demanded fire without price. Tamsin reveals she was born in the Spire's shadow. Emotional beat: found family forming around shared guilt.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Halvard corners them, offering to spare Wren if Ivo hands over the amulet — the covenant's anchor. Ivo refuses; Tamsin takes a wound meant for him. Halvard reveals the crown extinguished the first flame deliberately. Emotional beat: duty revealed as rot.

chapters.title: Ascent to the Guttering Light
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The climb up the Spire as the last dragon-fire gutters; the dead grow louder in Ivo's bones, nearly consuming him. Wren confesses she isn't the covenant's heir — she's its remainder, what was left when everything else burned. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness intertwined.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the flame's edge, Halvard attacks; Tamsin holds him off while Ivo understands the price: the covenant needs a living voice willingly given. He offers his own — his gift, his speech, his self — carving his final words into bone for Wren to read aloud. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Spire
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, closing with Ivo's. The flame accepts Ivo's voice; the covenant reforges, dragons' echoes joining his silence in a choir only Wren can hear. Ivo survives, mute, learning to speak with his hands beside his new family. Emotional beat: quiet, earned homecoming.
